verses.text: Paul, an apostle—not sent by people or appointed through a human being, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Jesus from the dead—
and all the brothers and sisters with me, to the churches in Galatia:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,
who gave himself for our sins to rescue us from this present evil age, in keeping with the will of our God and Father.
To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
I'm shocked that you're turning away so quickly from the one who called you by Christ's grace and following a different message.
There's no other Good News. Some people are confusing you and trying to twist Christ's Good News.
But even if we—or an angel from heaven—preach a different message than the one we preached to you, let them be condemned.
We've said it before, and I'll say it again: if anyone preaches a different message than the one you received, let them be condemned.
Am I trying to win people's approval or God's? Am I trying to please people? If I were still trying to please people, I wouldn't be Christ's servant.
Brothers and sisters, I want you to know that the Good News I preached didn't come from a human source.
I didn't receive it from a person or get taught it by one. It came through a revelation from Jesus Christ.
You've heard how I used to live in Judaism: I persecuted God's church viciously and tried to destroy it.
I advanced in Judaism beyond many of my own age and people, because I was even more devoted to my ancestors' traditions.
But God, who set me apart before I was born and called me by his grace,
was pleased to reveal his Son in me so I could preach him among the Gentiles. I didn't immediately consult with anyone,
or go to Jerusalem to see those who were apostles before me. Instead, I went to Arabia, then returned to Damascus.
After three years, I went up to Jerusalem to visit Cephas and stayed with him for fifteen days.
I didn't see any other apostles—only James, the Lord's brother.
I'm telling you the truth before God; I'm not lying about what I'm writing.
After that, I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
The churches in Judea that are in Christ still didn't know me personally.
They had only heard, ‘The man who once persecuted us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy.’
And they praised God because of me.
After fourteen years, I went back to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and I brought Titus along too.
I went because of a revelation. I explained the Good News I preach among the Gentiles privately to the leaders, to make sure I wasn't running—or had run—in vain.
But Titus, who was with me and was Greek, wasn't forced to be circumcised.
That came up because some false believers had secretly slipped in to spy on the freedom we have in Christ Jesus and to make us slaves.
We didn't give in to them—not even for a moment—so the truth of the Good News could remain with you.
As for those who seemed important (what they were makes no difference to me; God doesn't play favorites), those leaders added nothing to my message.
On the contrary, they saw that I had been entrusted with the Good News for the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been entrusted with the Good News for the circumcised.
For the one who worked through Peter as an apostle to the circumcised also worked through me among the Gentiles.

James, Cephas, and John—the leaders who were recognized as pillars—saw the grace given to me and offered Barnabas and me the hand of fellowship. We would go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.
They asked only that we remember the poor, which I was already eager to do.
But when Cephas came to Antioch, I confronted him face to face, because he was clearly in the wrong.
Before some people arrived from James, he ate with the Gentiles. But when they came, he pulled back and separated himself, afraid of the circumcision group.
The other Jews joined him in this hypocrisy, and even Barnabas was swept along with them.

When I saw they weren't acting in line with the truth of the Good News, I said to Cephas in front of everyone, ‘If you, a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, why are you forcing Gentiles to live like Jews?’
‘We are Jews by birth, not Gentile sinners,

yet we know a person is made right not by doing the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ. We too believed in Christ Jesus so we could be made right through faith in Christ, not by works of the law, because no one will be made right by doing those works.
But if we seek to be made right in Christ and are still found to be sinners, does that make Christ a servant of sin? Absolutely not!
If I rebuild what I tore down, I prove that I am a lawbreaker.
Through the law I died to the law, so I could live for God.
I have been crucified with Christ. It's no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. The life I now live in this body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
I don't set aside God's grace. If righteousness came through the law, then Christ died for nothing!’
You foolish Galatians! Who put a spell on you? Jesus Christ was clearly portrayed to you as crucified.
Tell me this: Did you receive the Spirit by doing what the law requires, or by hearing and believing?
Are you really this foolish? You began by the Spirit—are you now trying to finish by human effort?
Did you go through so much for nothing? Was it really for nothing?
Does God give you the Spirit and work miracles among you because you do what the law requires, or because you hear and believe?
In the same way, Abraham ‘believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.’
So understand this: those who have faith are Abraham's children.
Scripture foresaw that God would make the Gentiles right through faith, and announced the Good News to Abraham in advance: ‘All nations will be blessed through you.’
So those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.
Everyone who relies on doing what the law requires is under a curse. Scripture says, ‘Cursed is everyone who doesn't keep doing everything written in the book of the law.’
It's clear that no one is made right with God through the law, because Scripture says, ‘The righteous will live by faith.’
But the law isn't based on faith. It says, ‘The one who does these things will live by them.’
Christ rescued us from the law's curse by becoming a curse for us. Scripture says, ‘Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.’
He did this so Abraham's blessing could reach the Gentiles through Christ Jesus, and so that through faith we could receive the promised Spirit.
Brothers and sisters, let me use a human example: once a person's covenant is confirmed, no one can cancel it or add conditions to it.
The promises were made to Abraham and his descendant. Scripture doesn't say ‘to descendants,’ as if it meant many, but ‘to your descendant’—meaning Christ.
Here's what I mean: the law, which came 430 years later, doesn't cancel the covenant God had already confirmed, or nullify the promise.
If the inheritance came through the law, it wouldn't come through a promise. But God freely gave it to Abraham by promise.
So why was the law given? It was added because of wrongdoing, until the descendant came to whom the promise was made. Angels delivered it through a mediator.
But a mediator represents more than one party, while God is one.
So is the law against God's promises? Absolutely not! If a law had been given that could make people alive, then righteousness would indeed come through the law.
But Scripture has locked everything under sin, so that the promise through faith in Jesus Christ could be given to those who believe.
Before faith came, the law kept us in custody, locked up until the faith that was coming would be revealed.
So the law became our guardian until Christ came, so we could be made right through faith.
But now that faith has come, we're no longer under a guardian.
Through faith in Christ Jesus, you are all God's children.
All of you who were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
There is no Jew or Greek, slave or free, male and female. You are all one in Christ Jesus.
And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's descendants and heirs according to the promise.
As long as an heir is a child, they're no different from a slave, even though they own everything.
They remain under guardians and managers until the date their father set.
It's the same for us: when we were children, we were enslaved to the basic principles of this world.
But when the right time came, God sent his Son, born of a woman and born under the law,
to rescue those under the law so we could be adopted as God's children.
Because you are his children, God sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, ‘Abba! Father!’
So you are no longer a slave but a child. And if you are a child, you are also an heir through God.
Before, when you didn't know God, you were enslaved to things that aren't really gods.
But now you know God—or, better, God knows you—so why are you turning back to those weak and empty principles? Do you want to be enslaved by them all over again?
You carefully observe special days, months, seasons, and years.
I'm afraid I've wasted my effort on you.
Brothers and sisters, I beg you: become like me, because I became like you. You haven't wronged me.
You know that it was because of a physical illness that I first preached the Good News to you.
Even though my condition was a trial for you, you didn't reject or despise me. You welcomed me as an angel from God—as Christ Jesus himself.
What happened to the joy you had then? I can testify that, if it had been possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.
So have I become your enemy by telling you the truth?
Those people are eager to win you over, but not for your good. They want to separate you from us so you'll be eager to follow them.
It's always good to be eager for a good purpose, not only when I'm with you.
My dear children, I'm in labor pains for you all over again until Christ is formed in you.
I wish I could be with you now and change my tone, because I don't know what to make of you.
Tell me, you who want to live under the law: do you really listen to what the law says?
Scripture says Abraham had two sons, one by a slave woman and one by a free woman.
The son of the slave woman was born in the ordinary human way, but the son of the free woman was born through God's promise.
This story can be read as an allegory: the women represent two covenants. One covenant comes from Mount Sinai and gives birth to slavery; this is Hagar.
Hagar represents Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to present-day Jerusalem, which is in slavery along with her children.
But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.

Scripture says, ‘Rejoice, you who were unable to have children and never gave birth. Break into joyful shouting, you who never had labor pains. The woman left alone will have more children than the woman with a husband.’
Brothers and sisters, you are children of the promise, like Isaac.
At that time, the son born in the ordinary human way persecuted the son born through the Spirit. It's the same now.
But what does Scripture say? ‘Send away the slave woman and her son. The slave woman's son will never share the inheritance with the free woman's son.’
So, brothers and sisters, we aren't children of the slave woman. We are children of the free woman.
Christ set us free so we could live in freedom. So stand firm, and don't let anyone tie you up again in slavery.
Listen, I, Paul, am telling you: if you get circumcised as a requirement, Christ won't benefit you.
I testify again to every man who gets circumcised: he is obligated to obey the whole law.
You who are trying to be made right by the law have cut yourselves off from Christ; you've fallen away from grace.
But through the Spirit, by faith, we eagerly wait for the hope of righteousness.
In Christ Jesus, circumcision and uncircumcision mean nothing. What matters is faith expressing itself through love.
You were running a great race! Who cut in on you and kept you from obeying the truth?
That kind of persuasion doesn't come from the one who called you.
A little yeast spreads through the whole batch.
I'm confident in the Lord that you'll come around to the right view. But whoever is confusing you will face judgment, whoever they are.
Brothers and sisters, if I still preached circumcision, why am I still persecuted? Then the cross wouldn't be a stumbling block anymore.
I wish those who are upsetting you would go all the way and mutilate themselves!
You were called to freedom, brothers and sisters. But don't use your freedom to indulge your human nature. Instead, serve one another through love.
The whole law is summed up in one command: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’
But if you keep biting and devouring one another, watch out or you'll destroy each other.
So I say: live by the Spirit, and you won't carry out the desires of your human nature.
Our human nature desires what opposes the Spirit, and the Spirit desires what opposes our human nature. They're opposed to each other, so you can't just do whatever you want.
But if the Spirit leads you, you're not under the law.
The works of our human nature are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity, and reckless behavior;
idolatry, sorcery, hatred, fighting, jealousy, angry outbursts, selfish ambition, division, and factions;
envy, murder, drunkenness, wild partying, and things like these. I'm warning you, as I warned you before: people who practice such things won't inherit God's Kingdom.
But the Spirit produces love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
gentleness, and self-control. There is no law against these things.
Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified their human nature, along with its passions and desires.
Since we live by the Spirit, let's keep in step with the Spirit too.
Let's not become conceited, provoking and envying one another.
Brothers and sisters, if someone is caught in any wrongdoing, you who are led by the Spirit should gently help them get back on track. Watch yourself too, so you aren't tempted.
Carry one another's burdens, and in this way you'll fulfill Christ's law.
If anyone thinks they're important when they're not, they're fooling themselves.
Each person should examine their own work. Then they can take pride in their own actions, without comparing themselves to someone else.
Each person will carry their own load.
Anyone who is taught the word should share all good things with their teacher.
Don't fool yourselves: God can't be mocked. A person harvests whatever they plant.
Those who plant for their human nature will harvest decay from it. Those who plant for the Spirit will harvest eternal life from the Spirit.
Let's not get tired of doing good. At the right time we'll harvest a crop if we don't give up.
So whenever we have the opportunity, let's do good to everyone, especially to those who belong to the family of believers.
Look at the large letters I'm using as I write this greeting in my own hand.
Those who want to make a good impression by human standards are pressuring you to be circumcised. They do it only to avoid being persecuted for the cross of Christ.
Even those who are circumcised don't keep the law themselves. They want you circumcised so they can brag about your bodies.
But I will never brag about anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ. Through that cross, the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
In Christ Jesus, circumcision or uncircumcision means nothing. What matters is being made new.
Peace and mercy to all who follow this rule, and to God's Israel.
From now on, don't let anyone trouble me, because I carry on my body the marks of Jesus.
Brothers and sisters, may the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
